questionStem: The normal distribution is a fundamental concept in statistics because:
options: Many real-world biological and psychological phenomena approximate it.
It has a mean of 0 and a standard deviation of 1.
It can be used to describe any type of dataset.
correctOptionText: Many real-world biological and psychological phenomena approximate it.

In a perfectly normal distribution, the mean, median, and mode are:
options: Located at different points on the x-axis.
Equal and located at the center of the distribution.
Used to calculate the standard deviation.
correctOptionText: Equal and located at the center of the distribution.

options: In the top 1.5% of all values.

questionStem: The Standard Normal Distribution is defined as having:
options: A mean of 1 and a standard deviation of 0.
A mean of 0 and a standard deviation of 1.
Any mean and a standard deviation of 1.
correctOptionText: A mean of 0 and a standard deviation of 1.

questionStem: To convert a raw score (X) to a Z-score, you must:
options: Multiply the raw score by the standard deviation.
Subtract the mean from the raw score and divide by the standard deviation.
Add the mean to the raw score and multiply by the standard deviation.
Divide the raw score by the mean.
correctOptionText: Subtract the mean from the raw score and divide by the standard deviation.

questionStem: A medical student scores 88 on a test. The class average is 80 with a standard deviation of 4. What is the student's Z-score?

options: Are heavier than the tails of other distributions.
Approach but never touch the horizontal axis.
correctOptionText: Approach but never touch the horizontal axis.

questionStem: The Central Limit Theorem is important in hypothesis testing because it:
options: Proves that all data is normally distributed.
Allows the use of normal distribution-based tests with large sample sizes, even if the original data isn't normal.
States that the mean is always the best measure of central tendency.
Calculates the standard deviation for any dataset.
correctOptionText: Allows the use of normal distribution-based tests with large sample sizes, even if the original data isn't normal.

questionStem: Which of the following is a common application of the normal distribution in medicine?
options: Modeling the distribution of a rare disease's incidence across many cities.
Describing the distribution of human lifespans.
Representing the range of normal values for a lab test like fasting blood glucose in a healthy population.
Charting the number of patients arriving at the ER each hour, which can be highly variable.
correctOptionText: Representing the range of normal values for a lab test like fasting blood glucose in a healthy population.

questionStem: A limitation of the normal distribution is that:
options: It cannot be used for statistical inference.
Not all real-world data follows its pattern, such as heavily skewed data.
It is only applicable to social sciences.
It overestimates the probability of outliers.
correctOptionText: Not all real-world data follows its pattern, such as heavily skewed data.

options: Fewer outliers than a normal distribution.
A flatter peak than a normal distribution.
More outliers than a normal distribution.
correctOptionText: More outliers than a normal distribution.

questionStem: The Empirical Rule states that 99.7% of data in a normal distribution fall within how many standard deviations of the mean?
If a set of lab results for a hormone level is normally distributed, we can expect that about 68% of the results will lie between:
options: The mean and one standard deviation above the mean.
One standard deviation below and one standard deviation above the mean.
Two standard deviations below and two standard deviations above the mean.
correctOptionText: One standard deviation below and one standard deviation above the mean.

questionStem: The formula Z = \frac{x - \mu}{\sigma} is used to:
options: Calculate the variance of a population.
Find the probability of a specific value, x.
Standardize a value from any normal distribution to a standard normal scale.
Calculate the mean of a sample.
correctOptionText: Standardize a value from any normal distribution to a standard normal scale.

questionStem: In a normal distribution of heart rates, a Z-score of 0 corresponds to a heart rate that is:
options: One standard deviation above the mean.

questionStem: Which of the following phenomena would LEAST likely follow a normal distribution?
options: IQ scores of a large, random group of adults.
Survival time after diagnosis for a terminal cancer with a very poor prognosis.
Measurement errors in a calibrated lab instrument.
correctOptionText: Survival time after diagnosis for a terminal cancer with a very poor prognosis.

In quality control for manufacturing medical devices, the normal distribution is often used to model:
options: The number of devices that fail completely.
The variability in product measurements, like the diameter of a stent.
The yes/no outcome of a device passing inspection.
The time until a device fails.
correctOptionText: The variability in product measurements, like the diameter of a stent.

correctOptionText: Significantly higher than the population average.

questionStem: In a research study, the 95% confidence interval for the mean diastolic blood pressure is calculated as (78, 82). This interval is based on the properties of the normal distribution and means:
options: 95% of the sample population has a diastolic blood pressure between 78 and 82.
We are 95% confident that the true population mean diastolic blood pressure lies between 78 and 82.
There is a 5% probability that the mean is below 78.
The standard deviation of the sample is 4.
correctOptionText: We are 95% confident that the true population mean diastolic blood pressure lies between 78 and 82.

Proves that the empirical rule is true for any dataset.
correctOptionText: Allows us to assume the sample mean is normally distributed if the sample size is large enough, even if the original data is not.

questionStem: A leptokurtic distribution of a biomarker in a population would suggest a higher probability of:
options: Values very close to the mean.
Values evenly distributed across the range.

correctOptionText: Extreme values (outliers) compared to a normal distribution.

correctOptionText: The sampling distribution of the test statistic.

correctOptionText: To generalize from a sample to a population and test hypotheses

Generalizing findings from a sample to a population

correctOptionText: Sampling variation and the fact we usually only take one sample

questionStem: The Central Limit Theorem primarily describes the relationship between:
options: Sample statistics and their corresponding population parameters
The mean and the mode of a sample
correctOptionText: Sample statistics and their corresponding population parameters

questionStem: According to the Central Limit Theorem, if we take many samples of size n from a population, the distribution of the sample means will be:

options: The variability within a single sample

options: More tightly clustered around the population mean
More spread out from the population mean

correctOptionText: More spread out from the population mean

options: A definitive proof for our research hypothesis
An exact value for the population parameter

correctOptionText: A range of values (confidence interval) for the population parameter
